rows.A_note: EV-100 to EV-102 show a chartered committee meeting quarterly with recorded decisions (6 of 9 with a named owner). Anchor 2 also requires the committee to review AI strategy, and EV-103 shows strategy is not on its agenda. Not 2 for that reason. Level 3 elements are partly present, but a missing level 2 element cannot be offset by them.
rows.B_note: Chartered executive committee with scheduled meetings, decisions logged (EV-100/EV-102); strategy not reviewed by committee so not level 3.

rows.A_note: Absence is established, not just unaddressed. EV-120 shows the dashboard has no AI-role breakdown, EV-121 shows no AI-specific hiring analysis, and EV-122 shows no action plan and no promotion analysis. No non-discrimination policy is named in the pack, so anchor 1 is not evidenced. The all-staff dashboard is not AI-role representation data. Would be 1 if an approved non-discrimination policy were
rows.B_note: No AI-specific diversity evidence; general dashboard and hiring review do not address control applicability; absence not explicitly evidenced.

rows.A_note: EV-171 is individual-driven informal collaboration with no agreement, which matches the Level 1 anchor and rules out Level 0. EV-170 confirms there are no formal partnerships, agreements or publications, so Level 2 is not met. EV-170 and EV-171 are consistent, not conflicting: formal absent, informal present.
rows.B_note: Evidence explicitly states absence of any research collaborations or agreements.

rows.A_note: EV-620, EV-621 and EV-623 would support Level 2 or 3 for the 14 registered systems. Level 2 requires a recorded decision for every deployment, and EV-622 shows two clinical pilots deployed with no decision record (2026-07). Level 3 therefore cannot be credited, and Level 2 is only partially satisfied.
rows.B_note: Formal go/no-go process and records for most deployments; two clinical pilots without records preclude Level 3.

rows.A_note: A documented procedure with triage, recovery and a lessons log exists (EV-680) and was used once with a recovery record and lessons entry (EV-681). The pack does not state the procedure's scope; I read it as org-wide, and if it is CTA-only this drops to 1. Level 3 is not met: the lessons log has 1 entry, with no review cadence and no detection, response-time or closure metrics (EV-682). Non-exerci
rows.B_note: Procedure and lessons log exist but not for all systems; no review cadence or repeated use.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: tested for all 14 systems in the 2026-06 game day (EV-692). Responsibility is named explicitly only for CTA (Model Owner, EV-690), and I treated that as a role-based assignment. Level 3 is met by measured time-to-deactivate per system (median 6 min, worst 22 min) against a 30-minute target (EV-693). Level 4 is not met: there is no failsafe or automated disengagement and no independ
rows.B_note: Tested deactivation mechanisms and responsibilities exist for all systems, including vendor cases.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met for the 4 critical vendors: monitoring is scheduled, SLA reports are collected, and issues are logged and closed (4 of 6). The anchor has no 'every vendor' wording, so I did not apply it. Level 3 is not met: there is no evidence of review against contractual thresholds, and no contract review since onboarding (EV-702). Gaps: 5 lower-spend vendors are unmonitored and 2 issues are ove
rows.B_note: Monitoring only covers critical vendors, not all; no contract reviews since onboarding.

rows.A_note: Level 2 requires performance assessed on each update, and 1 of 3 2026 updates (2026-09) was applied without evaluation. The inventory covers all 14 systems and tracks versions (EV-710, EV-712). The Level 3 artefact is present (monthly drift and regression review, EV-713), but Level 3 builds on Level 2. If the 2026-09 update is shown to have been evaluated, for example by the drift-triggered re-eva
rows.B_note: Drift and regression metrics per model are reviewed monthly and trigger actions.

rows.A_note: The backlog is linked to monitoring findings and release notes cite the triggering finding (EV-730, EV-731), which clearly exceeds Level 1. Stakeholder-input and best-practice-capture artefacts are not named in the pack, which is a weakness at Level 2. Level 3 is partial: throughput is tracked, but measured effect per release exists for only 7 of 9 releases (EV-732).
rows.B_note: Throughput and effect per release tracked for 7/9 releases.

rows.A_note: A register with communication actions exists (EV-740), but stakeholder communication is not defined: there is no time-to-notify target and no AI-incident templates (EV-742). One of 3 notifiable incidents was kept internal on the incident lead's discretion (EV-741). Recovery documentation is not shown in this pack. Level 2 is not fully met.
rows.B_note: Incident communication and register exist, but no reviewed metrics or cadence evidence.

rows.A_note: Competencies are documented per role family (EV-210) rather than per project. The staffing checklist is signed off for 1 of 4 projects, so composition review against requirements is partial. EV-212 shows no diversity metric, which is not itself an anchor 2 or 3 requirement.
rows.B_note: Documented competency requirements and review for one project, framework exists.

rows.A_note: L2 is not fully met. The 22 socio-technical requirements exist (EV-250) with workshop input (EV-252), but none are traced to tests, only 96 of 148 requirements are traced overall, and stakeholder input is attributed for only 41. Partial L2 scores L1.
rows.B_note: Level 3 not met: traceability to tests does not cover socio-technical requirements (EV-251); only 96/148 requirements traced to test case.

rows.A_note: For CTA, limits, out-of-scope claim types and the oversight requirement are documented (EV-270) and enforced in configuration (EV-271, export 2026-09-12). The L2 anchor does not require every system, so the CTA-only coverage in EV-272 is recorded here rather than used to cap the score. L3 artefacts (measured refusal rate, guardrail coverage per release) are absent.
rows.B_note: Level 2 not met: knowledge limits and enforced oversight are documented only for CTA, not all systems (EV-272).

rows.A_note: L2 requires proficiency requirements, an assessment process and certification requirements. The standard and assessment method exist (EV-320) and 34 of 61 adjusters are assessed (EV-321), but there is no certification requirement and no refresher cycle (EV-322). Partial L2 scores L1.
rows.B_note: Level 3 not met: proficiency assessment not tracked/reported across full population (34 of 61 assessed), and no certification process (EV-322).

rows.A_note: EV-370 plan, EV-371 records and EV-372 changes log are ML3-type artefacts, but records exist for only 4 of 6 planned sessions. The pack does not say whether the other 2 were held. EV-373 shows the member panel came from the existing customer council, not a sample of affected members. Would be 2 if the 2 sessions are shown not yet due. No ML4 engagement-effectiveness metrics are present.
rows.B_note: Systematic engagement with participant records and a log of changes for most sessions.

rows.A_note: EV-413 (annual re-validation completed 2026-09) and EV-411 (dated validation study that found a 1.8x under-count) support systematic assessment. EV-412's per-metric FP/FN analysis and revision history would be the distinguishing artefact for the next level, but it is undated and conflicts with EV-410 (limits documented for 4 of 9 metrics) and EV-411 (one study). I did not accept it as current evid
rows.B_note: Revision history and false-positive/-negative analysis for all metrics, reviewed and documented.

rows.A_note: EV-430 and EV-431 meet ML3 for current runs. EV-432 shows 3 of 12 evaluations lack manifests, recorded as a defect, so 'every evaluation' is not fully met. EV-432 is the reproducibility measurement (2026-09) that distinguishes ML4. Would be 3 if the legacy runs are remediated or shown out of scope.
rows.B_note: Reproducibility measured (9 of 12) and reported; full anchor 3 met.

rows.A_note: CTA evidence meets ML3 (EV-530, EV-531) and the next level's tracking artefact (EV-533, three releases against thresholds, with a 2026-07 breach remediated). EV-534 states other in-scope systems have no fairness evaluation, so 'per system' fails. Would be 3 for CTA alone. No intersectional analysis, continuous monitoring or public reporting for ML5.
rows.B_note: Comprehensive fairness evaluation and mitigations for CTA, but no regular tracking or inclusion of other systems.

rows.A_note: EV-550 (2026-09) records coverage 62%, 3 post-release defects and two process changes, but EV-551 shows metric effectiveness assessed for only 2 of 9 metrics. EV-552 shows scope is CTA only. 'Systematic' is not evidenced beyond one review. The coverage and defect figures cover one cycle, not tracked per cycle, so the next level is not supported either.
rows.B_note: TEVV effectiveness systematically reviewed for CTA, with defects and improvements recorded; cycle-based tracking or coverage for wider programme not fully evidenced.

rows.A_note: EV-440 shows no human-subject evaluation was run in the period, so the control was not triggered and the ML1 anchor (evaluations run without ethics review) cannot be established. EV-441 and EV-442 show no ethics process or consent records exist. Would score 0 if a human-subject study were in scope, for example a study behind the adjuster-trust criterion in EV-452.
rows.B_note: Evidence explicitly shows absence of human-subject evaluation, ethics review or consent processes.

rows.A_note: L2 met (EV-460, all 14 in-scope systems, drift and output-distribution anomaly detection). L3 met (EV-462, precision/recall and alert-to-action time reviewed monthly by the AI Operations Council). L4 not fully met. EV-463 shows predictive alerting and threshold re-sets from incident data, but no real-time dashboard is named in the pack. EV-463 dates the incident analysis to 2026-05, while EV-461 l
rows.B_note: Predictive alerting and real-time dashboards optimised from measured incidents evidenced by dated artefacts.

rows.A_note: Between L1 and L2. Test-retest reliability exists (EV-470, kappa 0.81), but generalisability rests on one held-out region and two regions were excluded for small samples (EV-471). Inter-labeler reliability was not assessed (EV-472). L2 is only partially met, so it scores L1.
rows.B_note: Validity and reliability (with some generalisability) documented; reliability across labelers not assessed, no ongoing tracking.
